newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia central bank head sees bank closures.
newsitem.headline: Latvia central bank head sees bank closures.

text.p: Latvian central bank chief Einar Repshe on Wednesday said he expected more bank closures and mergers next year as banks were obliged to meet higher capital requirements.
In an interview with Reuters, he also said that he believed the lat was slightly undervalued but was happy with the Baltic state's economic and monetary policies.
Repshe noted that by the end of March next year banks will have to increase their capital to two million lats ($3.4 million) from one million lats.
"It is possible that three to five banks will be closed in a civilised manner through this process," Repshe said.
Repshe also said he saw three to five bank merger cases as banks got together to boost capital.
The central bank in Latvia, hit in 1995 by a severe bank crisis, has sharply toughened bank regulation and supervision.
There are still some 33 banks in the country, which has a population of 2.7 million although the central bank recently said it has started proceedings to withdraw the licence of Latvian privatbanka.
Repshe also said that he put the stability of the lat, pegged at 0.7997 to the SDR, high on his list of priorities and said there would be no change in the currency arrangement.
"My guess is that the lat is still slightly undervalued," he said.
He said that in nominal terms the currency would not change but that in real terms as inflation differentials between Latvia and the rest of the world narrow, the lat could appreciate in value.
